records.summary: 1463 Haight St sits in the Haight Street NCD-HAIGHT zoning district, where restaurants on the first story are principally permitted, but the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict requires Conditional Use Authorization for any new on-sale liquor establishment (ABC Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57) serving alcohol. The site was approved as a limited restaurant with no alcohol in December 2017; converting to a full-service restaurant with alcohol is a change of use. The block is heavily saturated: 17 food and drink businesses within 500 ft, 6 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft and 16 within 1,000 ft, triggering the undue-concentration flag. Only three dated use decisions for similar concepts have been filed within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years—too few to compute an approval rate—but nearby restaurant applications with alcohol have been approved, including one just 13 meters away in September 2024 for the same limited-to-full-service upgrade.

patterns.pattern: Before Board Ordinance 249-23 (enacted 2023), restaurants in the Haight Street NCD added ABC Type 41 (beer and wine) licenses via simple agency referral without Conditional Use Authorization, approved in 1–20 days. After Ordinance 249-23, any new on-sale alcohol license in the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict requires a CUA hearing.

The September 2024 CUA approval at 1457 Haight for the identical limited-to-full restaurant change imposed only standard Planning Commission conditions (three-year validity, community liaison, sidewalk maintenance) with no special restrictions on hours, capacity, security, or sound, and passed 7-0.

Planning approved ABC Type 41 and Type 23 licenses for existing restaurants as continuations of use, but denied a Type 01 (off-sale only) license at 1390 Haight because off-sale alcohol sales are inconsistent with restaurant use in the NCD-HAIGHT district.

Full-service restaurants with alcohol in NCD-HAIGHT have historically required Conditional Use Authorization even before Ordinance 249-23: a 2010 CUA (Motion No. 18079) was cited as the basis for a restaurant's continued operation in 2020.

Once a restaurant use is established in NCD-HAIGHT, continuations and ownership changes are approved administratively via agency referral (Health, ABC) in 1–30 days unless the use intensifies (e.g., adding alcohol, expanding hours, changing from limited to full-service).

findings.text: 1463 Haight St sits in zoning district NCD-HAIGHT, where a restaurant on the first story is principally permitted under Planning Code Section 719 (in force from January 14, 2024, Ordinance 249-23).

The Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict requires Conditional Use Authorization for any new on-sale liquor establishment (ABC Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57) per Planning Code Section 781.9(c)(2), in force from January 14, 2024 (Ordinance 249-23).
This address was approved in December 2017 as a limited restaurant with the explicit restriction that no alcohol is permitted on-site under Planning Code Section 202.2(a).
Converting from limited restaurant to full-service restaurant is a change of use under Planning Code Section 102 with the last use as described.

At 1457 Haight St, 13 meters away in the same district, Planning approved a Conditional Use Authorization in September 2024 for the identical change (limited to full-service restaurant, no construction) under Section 719 and Ordinance 249-23; the Commission passed it 7-0 with standard conditions only.

Before Ordinance 249-23 (enacted 2023), nearby restaurants at 1419, 1466, and 1401 Haight added ABC Type 41 (beer and wine) licenses via agency referral without CUA in 1–20 days; after 2023 all new on-sale licenses in the alcohol subdistrict require CUA.

approvals.summary: The rules could not decide which ABC licence is required because the alcohol type (beer and wine, or full liquor) and how the licence will be obtained (new or transfer) were not given; the Haight alcohol subdistrict requires CUA for any new on-sale licence.

findings.text: The Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict requires Conditional Use Authorization for any new on-sale liquor establishment (ABC Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57) per Planning Code Section 781.9(c)(2).
Six active ABC on-sale licenses exist within 500 ft (Types 17, 48, 41, 20, 41, 41) and 16 total within 1,000 ft, triggering the density undue-concentration flag.

ABC licence applications for any type are sent to the Police Department ABC Liaison Unit and to the Planning Department for review; these are referral steps inside the ABC application, not separate approvals.
At 1390 Haight St, 131 meters away, Planning denied an ABC Type 01 (off-sale) referral in May 2021 because it did not fit restaurant use per Section 102, but stated Type 23 would be approvable.

approvals.summary: Limited restaurant to restaurant is a change of use requiring a building permit that must conform to the Planning Code; the building code change of occupancy is not established because the occupant load is not given, so further review is required.

findings.text: Limited restaurant to restaurant is a change of use under Planning Code Section 102 with the last use as described.
Under the Building Code a restaurant or bar is Assembly Group A-2, and a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B; the proposed occupancy group depends on the occupant load, which is not given.
The existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records; only plans or an inspection show it, so a change of occupancy is not established.
A change of use needs a building permit, and the permit must conform to the Planning Code before it is issued.
Building permit applications are sent to the Planning Department for review as a referral step inside the building permit, not a separate approval.

expected_conditions.condition: Three-year validity: the authorization expires three years from the effective date unless a building or site permit is issued within that period.
expected_conditions.basis: The September 2024 CUA at 1457 Haight for the same limited-to-full upgrade imposed standard three-year validity per Planning Code Section 186.1. This is the Commission's standard condition for all CUAs.

expected_conditions.condition: Community liaison: before issuing a building permit the project sponsor must appoint a community liaison officer and provide written notice of the name, business address and telephone number to the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups.
expected_conditions.basis: The September 2024 CUA at 1457 Haight imposed this standard community liaison condition. The Commission applies it to most conditional uses in residential and mixed-use districts.

expected_conditions.condition: Sidewalk maintenance: the project sponsor must maintain the main entrance and all sidewalks abutting the property in a clean and sanitary condition per Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards.
expected_conditions.basis: The September 2024 CUA at 1457 Haight imposed this standard sidewalk maintenance condition. It is a standard condition for all ground-floor commercial uses.

expected_conditions.condition: ABC Type 41 (beer and wine, eating place) or Type 47 (full liquor, eating place): no other licence type is permitted for a restaurant in this district.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning denied a Type 01 (off-sale) licence at 1390 Haight in 2021 as inconsistent with restaurant use per Section 102, and all nearby restaurant alcohol approvals are Type 41 or Type 47 (on-sale, eating place).

expected_conditions.condition: Continuation of restaurant use: operations must remain a bona fide eating place with meals prepared and served on-site; the alcohol licence may not be used for a bar or nightclub use.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2017 approval at this address required operation under Planning Code Section 202.2(a) conditions (limited restaurant), and nearby CUAs for restaurant alcohol distinguish eating places from bars. Planning Code Section 102 defines a restaurant as a retail use providing food and drink to patrons for consumption on the premises, with meals prepared in a kitchen.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the alcohol type (beer and wine only, or full liquor), chain status, and square footage with the applicant, then request a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to confirm whether a CUA is required.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The concept is a full-service restaurant with full cooking and alcohol at 1463 Haight St, converting from the limited restaurant approved in 2017 with no alcohol. The Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict requires CUA for new on-sale liquor, and the September 2024 CUA at 1457 Haight (13 meters away) approved the identical limited-to-full upgrade. We request confirmation that a CUA is the correct path and guidance on alcohol type, formula retail and size thresholds.

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning, including the project description, floor plans showing the dining area and kitchen, a menu, and the proposed ABC licence type.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The application is for a change of use from limited restaurant (approved December 2017, no alcohol) to full-service restaurant with alcohol under Planning Code Section 719 and Ordinance 249-23. No construction or expansion is proposed. The use will remain a bona fide eating place serving meals prepared on-site. Frame the application as consistent with the September 2024 approval at 1457 Haight for the same change, and commit to standard conditions (community liaison, three-year validity, sidewalk maintenance).

filing_playbook.action: Complete the pre-application community meeting (if required by Planning) and post the 300-foot notice at the property for 30 days before the Planning Commission hearing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Emphasize that the concept is a full-service restaurant with table service, not a bar or late-night use, and that alcohol is incidental to meals. Highlight the September 2024 approval 13 meters away for the same change, the lack of construction, and the commitment to maintain the neighborhood-serving character of the Haight corridor. Be prepared to address density concerns (17 food businesses and 6 on-sale licenses within 500 ft) by stressing the bona fide eating place requirement.

filing_playbook.action: Attend the Planning Commission hearing (1st and 3rd Thursdays) and present the application; the hearing is noticed to property owners within 300 feet and to registered neighborhood groups.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Present the concept as a full-service restaurant converting from the limited restaurant approved in 2017, with alcohol incidental to meals. Cite the September 2024 approval at 1457 Haight as directly comparable precedent and agree to standard conditions. If the census tract is flagged for undue concentration, explain that the restaurant will serve a Public Convenience or Necessity by providing a bona fide eating place with table service, not adding to bar density.

filing_playbook.action: If the CUA is approved, wait out the 30-day appeal period, then apply for the ABC licence (Type 41 for beer and wine, or Type 47 for full liquor) with the signed lease, California seller's permit, entity registration, and Planning's CUA approval letter.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the ABC application online with the CUA approval as zoning sign-off, the seller's permit, the signed lease, and the entity documents. Post the 30-day public notice at the premises as required by ABC. Frame the application as a bona fide eating place under ABC's requirements: meals prepared on-site, table service, kitchen facilities. If the census tract requires a Public Convenience or Necessity finding, coordinate with Planning and the Board of Supervisors for a PCN letter before ABC will issue.

filing_playbook.action: File the health permit application online with San Francisco Department of Public Health at least one month before opening, including the Business Account Number, Location ID, federal tax ID, menu, and the certified food safety manager certificate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The application is for a full-service restaurant with full cooking at 1463 Haight St. Attach the CUA approval, the menu showing meals prepared on-site, the equipment list, and the food safety manager certificate. Schedule the pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance and confirm all equipment, finishes, hand sinks, and hot water are in place per the DPH plan check.

filing_playbook.action: If a change of occupancy is required (depends on occupant load and existing occupancy group), file the building permit with plans stamped by an architect showing compliance with the Building Code occupancy group requirements.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The building permit is for a change of use from limited restaurant to full-service restaurant. If the occupant load is 50 or more, the occupancy group is Assembly A-2; if fewer than 50, it is Group B. Attach the CUA approval as zoning sign-off and coordinate with DPH plan check. If a change of occupancy is required, show ADA compliance, egress, and fire separation upgrades.

timeline_cost.notes: This is a time and cost to approval for the health permit and building permit (if required), which are the approvals in the entitlement path that the rules established. A Conditional Use Authorization—if one is required after the missing inputs are confirmed—would add 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 to this range (catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization is not in the path because the zoning row status is insufficient information). The 134–345 day range assumes the health permit (14–45 days, $470–$1,000) and a building permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000, plus prerequisite business registration 1–5 days, $55–$700, and health plan check 21–60 days, $828–$2,500, and food safety manager certificate 1–14 days, $100–$250). If the CUA is required the total timeline becomes 254–645 days and the cost becomes $7,316–$34,950. ABC licence time (60–240 days depending on type and transfer vs. new) and cost ($1,000–$450,000) are not included because the alcohol row status is insufficient information. No time or cost is given for formula retail, size over 2,500 sq ft, or hours triggers because those inputs are missing. State and federal registrations (EIN, entity, seller's permit, workers' comp, business registration certificate, fictitious business name) add 4–71 days and $185–$970 but can run in parallel. Music licenses (ASCAP, BMI) add 2–14 days and $600–$5,000. The September 2024 CUA at 1457 Haight took 106 days from filing to approval.
